decisions.executionNote: Raise left arm along elbow-up approach before aligning to the isolated left tube; right arm stays home.
Replan from guard stop with smaller orientation changes, moving left gripper above left tube.
Align downward left grasp with tube's long axis and descend to a pregrasp height.
Center on tube in wrist view, lower the last two centimeters, then close left gripper.
Lift left tube clear of table with closed gripper; verify visual retention before rotating upright.
Tube remains between left fingers. Rotate it toward upright while approaching the rack's left-side large slot.
Finish orienting held tube vertically over the left rack region, keeping clearance for visual slot alignment.
Lower upright tube toward left large slot, with a small backward alignment adjustment; retain grasp pending close view.
Continue slow vertical insertion into the aligned left hole, holding closed until depth is checked.
Tube did not visibly descend with the wrist, suggesting rim contact. Lift slightly and shift toward the front-left hole before retrying.
Lower the corrected tube and release over the left slot, then inspect whether it settles upright to depth.
Withdraw open left gripper to inspect the released tube while beginning an elbow-up right-arm approach to the outer right tube.
First tube is visibly seated upright. Return left arm away from rack while advancing right arm above the outer tube.
Orient the right gripper downward along the outer tube and approach pregrasp height; keep withdrawing left arm.
Refine right gripper alignment with the tube axis, descend to grasp, then close. Left arm approaches home.
Allow right fingers to close around the tube, then lift clear with grip maintained; finish left retreat near home.
Right tube is retained. Move toward the rack's rightmost large slot while rotating it upright with gradual elbow-up motion.
Continue the retained tube's upright rotation and approach to the right rack slot, maintaining clearance.
Finish upright alignment over the right slot, then begin a controlled vertical approach for close visual confirmation.
Lower the upright right tube toward its slot, watching for rim contact or sliding in the fingers.
Advance the right tube slowly to insertion depth, keeping the tube upright and monitoring for obstruction.
The tube appears supported on the rim rather than descending. Lift clear and shift slightly toward the front slot center before reseating.
Reseat the corrected right tube and open the gripper so it can settle into the slot; inspect before retreating.
Withdraw the open right gripper upward and backward to verify the second tube has settled, keeping clear of both inserted tubes.
The second tube did not remain seated. Clear the rack and approach the remaining original right tube; the displaced tube will need recovery.
Approach the original inner-right tube from above; displaced tube is visible on the table in front of the rack.
Finish aligning the open right gripper to the tube's axis and descend for a centered grasp.
Adjust grasp slightly toward the cap, close on the tube, and start lifting while checking retention.
Lift the retained tube fully clear, then turn it upright for a more precise placement into the middle large slot.
Carry the held tube toward the central front-row large hole, gradually rotating upright above the rack.
Complete upright alignment over the central rack hole, retaining enough height for a precise visual alignment before lowering.
Lower above the middle slot for close alignment, correcting the residual tilt; do not release until seating is visible.
Refine toward the front-row middle opening while lowering cautiously; watch for the tube remaining fixed against the rim.
The tube descended with the wrist. Continue a short, slow vertical insertion without lateral motion before releasing.
Tube cap is near the seated tube's height. Open in place and let it settle, keeping the wrist still to avoid disturbing the rack.
Middle tube appears seated beside the first. Withdraw the open right hand upward and backward before recovering the fallen tube.
Two tubes remain upright after withdrawal. Begin rotating the open right hand to match the fallen tube's reversed cap direction, above table clearance.
Continue gradual reverse-axis pregrasp rotation above the fallen tube, maintaining elbow-up continuity and clearance.
Continue the slow reverse-axis approach above the fallen tube, preserving configuration continuity and keeping the rack clear.
Finish the reversed downward grasp orientation and approach the fallen tube from above, leaving room for final visual centering.
Center the reverse-facing tube between the right fingers, shift slightly toward its cap, lower to grasp height, and close.
Finish closing on the recovered tube and lift vertically clear of the table before rotating it for insertion.
Recovered tube remains between the fingers. Raise for clearance and reverse the gradual wrist rotation to bring it upright over the remaining right slot.
Continue rotating the retained tube upright above the rack, keeping height to clear the two seated tubes.
Continue the slow upright rotation and move toward the empty right-side slot, keeping the recovered tube above its neighbors.
Finish the recovered tube's upright rotation and approach above the empty rightmost front-row hole.
Correct the small residual tilt and lower the recovered tube above the rightmost large opening, refining alignment before insertion.
Lower the recovered upright tube vertically toward the rightmost slot, keeping its axis fixed for close seating inspection.
Probe the right slot with a short slow vertical descent, checking whether the tube follows rather than sliding against the rim.
Partial sliding suggests front rim contact. Lift slightly and move one centimeter toward the rack interior, then retry the same height.
Test the corrected alignment with a slow two-centimeter descent; keep grasp closed and inspect tube motion.
